headline: Approved three road contracts: $2,594,728.25 for paving 36 streets, $2,572,326.00 for Arlington Neighborhood Street Scape, and $89,950 for pavement markings.
summary: Mayor Beauregard said the paving work is paid for with Fiscal Year 2026 capital funds and state Chapter 90 road money. Councilor DiZoglio asked about switching some hot mix sidewalks to concrete, an estimated extra $440,600, and the chair said that would need more money from the mayor, so the contract stayed as bid.
decisions: Approved $2,594,728.25 contract with EJ Paving Company for cold planing and paving of 36 streets, unanimously, 1 absent.
Approved $89,950.00 contract with K5 Corporation for pavement markings throughout Methuen, unanimously, 1 absent.
Approved $2,572,326.00 contract with PAO Corp. for Arlington Neighborhood Street Scape Phase 1, unanimously, 1 absent.

plain_text:
Methuen City Council – Special Meeting Minutes  
Thursday, August 13, 2026 – 5:00 pm 
Via Zoom Web Conference 
 
 
 
1. Roll Call – Members present – Clr. DiZoglio, Clr. Drew, Clr. MacLaren, Clr. 
Marsan, Clr. Santos, Clr. Simard, Clr. Valley and Chair Soto – Clr. Pesce absent  
 
2. Acceptance of the Agenda – Motion to accept the agenda by Clr. MacLaren, 
seconded by Clr. Santos – UPON ROLL CALL VOTE – unanimously approved, 1 
absent (Clr. Pesce) 
 
3. Public Participation – Linda Soucy, 10 Kirk Street, Methuen – “I wish to speak 
about utilizing the $2,572,326 in the Chapter 90 funds for the ARPA Phase 1 of the 
Arlington Neighborhood Streetscape Project. This funding is going to include all the 
roads that received infrastructure improvements over the past year and a half as part 
of Phase 1 ARPA project. It was Center Street, Anna Street, Camden Street, Ashton 
Place, and Chelmsford Street, all using ARPA funds to complete the first part of the 
project for Phase 1, and the only thing left, from what I understand, is the streetscape 
part of it. As someone who lives in the neighborhood, I think it's important to show 
each phase as completed, including the streetscapes. We have had roads in disrepair 
for many years, and it's only through this project that we're hoping to get them done. 
I would appreciate your vote on putting this forward, and thank you very much for 
your time. 
 
4.  Contracts: 
 
C-27-24- EJ Paving Company, Inc., 101 Lindberg Avenue, Methuen, MA 01844 – 
Cold Planing & Paving of 36 Streets provided by the City of Methuen - 
$2,594,728.25 - CIP FY25 $394,000.00, CIP FY26 $2,200,728.25 – Motion to 
approve by Clr. DiZoglio, seconded by Clr. Drew – Discussion – Chair Soto 
recognized Mayor Beauregard, “Thank you, Madam Chair. Just by way of 
introduction for the contracts on tonight's agenda. First of all, I apologize for the 
inconvenience of having to call a Special Meeting the same week as our meeting on 
Monday night. Just to provide some background, as I shared during the budget 
process, we had made some adjustments to the CIP for Fiscal Year 2026, which, of 
course, includes a $3.5 million allocation for fixes to our roads. Mainly, in essence, 
establishing a plan going forward where, in order to avoid the debt service payments 
on the Fiscal Year 2026, we decided to take any projects that had not been underway 
before July 1st, and, in essence, move them to implementation after July 1st, so that 
now the debt service payments for this bonding won't hit our budget until Fiscal Year 
2028. So, this was one of the measures that we took, trying to be creative with the 
Fiscal Year 2027 budget in order to free up money for various other things that, of 
course, we needed to take care of --- schools, City Hall departments, and the like, 
public safety, etc. So, in essence, that's why we're here now after the start of the fiscal 
year. We were out to bid for these contracts, lining up with that timeline. The bids 
closed on August 6th, which, of course, was after the agenda deadline for last 
Monday's agenda. So, we were able to get these contracts signed off on and 
presented tonight. We're using, as the funding sources, of course, the Fiscal Year 
2026 CIP for a significant bulk of it. We're also tapping into our Chapter 90 funds,

which the state provides us for road work and the like. So, we are in for a very busy 
couple of months here of extensive road work. We're going to be paving the entire 
length of Milk Street, for instance. One of the most run-down sections of Forest 
Street is being taken care of, along with numerous other residential areas. And, 
beyond that, there are several stretches of main roads, heavily traveled roads in the 
city. For instance, a great example is Pleasant Street. So Pleasant Street, in the area 
around the Tenney (School) and City Hall, was recently resurfaced, which is great, 
but there's a section as you're driving down the roadway, you get to Marston 
Corners, and there's a section of it right at the lights there. It's, in essence, like 
driving, frankly, along the surface of the moon. And so, although the entirety of the 
road doesn't need to be resurfaced, there are sections of roads that need to be 
resurfaced, especially the main ones. So, this will help us get after all of that. And 
again, a word of warning to residents that there will be likely disruptions in our 
neighborhoods as a result of this, but we'll be getting after quite a bit of work by way 
of these contracts. And this doesn't include another series of contracts that will be 
coming down the pipe as soon as well. We have bids closing on, I believe, over 50 
miles of cracked sealing. That bid will be closing in the coming weeks, so we'll get 
that to you in time for the next meeting. But I wanted to give you the context, the 
funding sources, and why we're here at a quirky time. And again, thank you for 
taking the time out of your day to go on with this.” Chair Soto said, “Excellent. I'm 
excited to see this happen. As we all know, this is one of the main concerns we get in 
Request for Constituents requests are their streets.” – UPON ROLL CALL VOTE – 
unanimously approved – 1 absent (Clr. Pesce) 
 
C-27-25 - K5 Corporation, 9 Rockview Way, Rockland, MA 02370 - Pavement 
Markings throughout the City of Methuen -$89,950.00 – Chapter 90 funds – Motion 
to approve by Clr. Santos, seconded by Clr. Drew – UPON ROLL CALL VOTE 
– unanimously approved – 1 absent (Clr. Pesce) 
 
C-27-26 - PAO Corp., 3 Sandy Knoll Drive, Hudson, MA 01749 - Arlington 
Neighborhood Street Scape Phase 1- $2,572,326.00 - Chap. 90 funds (waiting on 
Mayor's Docusign for this- Pat had texted Mayor about this.) Motion to approve by 
Clr. Santos, seconded by Clr. Drew – Discussion – Chair Soto recognized Mayor 
Beauregard, “Thank you, Madam Chair. Yeah, not sure why that ended up on the 
agenda as it did. My apologies. But we were able to get this one finalized for 
signatures on Tuesday. At the same time, we were on our way to Tanglewood out in 
the Berkshires to see Hugh Jackman and the Boston Pops. So, I had a Docusign it, 
but it's all good to go at this point.” Chair Soto recognized Clr. DiZoglio, “I just have 
one, and everybody knows what I'm going to say. It says here, and I appreciate Mr. 
Garcia for putting the bid for a substitute of hot mix, asphalt sidewalks to concrete 
was going to be an estimated additional $440,600 to basically do that whole area 
with concrete. And I just have a question for the Council --- we could really have a 
benefit of that neighborhood for an extra $440,000. I was just wondering if the 
Council would consider possibly substituting that. You know, in the investment. I 
just want to put the question out there. Would this be a benefit for us to vote on as a

substitute? And have anybody answer any questions funding wise?” Chair Soto said, 
“So, I guess that's something that you'd have to bring up to the Mayor, so he can 
appropriate some additional dollars, Councilor. For this line item, we would approve 
that as is to not have any further delays.” Chair Soto recognized Clr. Drew, “I was 
just going to mention 400 and some thousand dollars on top of the 13 million dollars 
we've already spent this year. I understand Councilor DiZoglio's thought process on 
the concrete. I completely agree with that. I just don't know if right now, financially, 
it makes any sort of sense. And to take that kind of extra money out of any 
stabilizations or things like that.” – UPON ROLL CALL VOTE – unanimously 
approved – 1 absent (Clr. Pesce) 
 
Motion to enter into Executive Session by Clr. Drew, seconded by Santos – UPON 
ROLL CALL VOTE – unanimously approved, 1 absent (Clr. Pesce) 
 
Respectfully submitted,  
Lisa Yarid Ferry 
Assistant City Council Clerk
